issue.title: MockitoJUnitRunner too strict by default?
issue.body:
In one of the projects being migrated to Mockito 2 I've observed that deprecated `org.mockito.runners.MockitoJUnitRunner` (tested with 2.11.0) works in a strict mode by default (fails a test on unnecessary stubbing). I wonder if it is an expected behavior?

Even Mockito rule works in a "warn" mode by default. It makes it a little bit harder to migrate from Mockito 1.10.x to 2.x.

input.args: Issue 1212: "MockitoJUnitRunner too strict by default?" Reporter migrating from Mockito 1.10 to 2.x. The deprecated org.mockito.runners.MockitoJUnitRunner (2.11.0) fails tests on unnecessary stubbing by default, while the MockitoRule (MockitoJUnit.rule()) only warns by default. Asks whether this is expected. Verified in source: MockitoJUnitRunner.java default constructor uses StrictRunner(createStrict); MockitoJUnitRunner.Silent is the opt-out and Strict/StrictStubs are variants; MockitoJUnit.rule() uses Strictness.WARN. Evidence files: mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/junit/MockitoJUnitRunner.java and mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/junit/MockitoJUnit.java.

final: {"number": 1212, "label": "question", "route": "answer", "related": [720, 384, 391], "evidence": ["mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/junit/MockitoJUnitRunner.java", "mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/junit/MockitoJUnit.java"], "reply": "Yes, this is by design. Since 2.1.0, MockitoJUnitRunner is strict by default: it reports unused stubs as failures (UnnecessaryStubbingException). MockitoJUnit.rule() defaults to warnings only (Strictness.WARN), which is why the two behave differently. To get the 1.x behaviour from the runner, annotate the test class with @RunWith(MockitoJUnitRunner.Silent.class). If you want the runner to also catch stubbing argument mismatches, use MockitoJUnitRunner.StrictStubs. The runner's Javadoc covers all three variants."}
